clue.text: 8's bloomers

parts.note: 8 down is a female ballet dancer; her bloomers are blunders, literally false steps, playing on the French word for a dance step

explanation.surface: A ballerina's baggy underwear, of the kind worn in old-fashioned dance classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like underwear but means blunders. A dancer's steps are 'pas' in French, so a dancer's blunder is a false step, which is what the French phrase literally says.
explanation.definitionFit: A social gaffe or blunder is a bloomer in British slang, and this French phrase means a false step.

clue.text: Distant game sounding very loud

parts.note: faro is an old gambling card game
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A remote match that can be heard as extremely noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remote in place or time is a long way away.

clue.text: Cow with a French sauce

parts.note: un is French for a
sauce is cheek, impudence, as is nerve

explanation.surface: A cow served with French dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' is the verb meaning intimidate, and 'sauce' means cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them, sapping their courage.

clue.text: Burning desire to copy Roman I admire to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An urge to imitate a Roman one looks up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning desire' sounds like a passion; literally it is an urge to set fires.
explanation.definitionFit: This compulsion is an obsessive urge to set fires.

clue.text: State of 5 dn, shortened then expanded

definitions.text: State of 5 dn, shortened then expanded

parts.words: State of 5 dn, shortened then expanded
parts.note: 5 down cut short leaves a two-letter country abbreviation, which written out in full names a nation

explanation.surface: A gloomy mood, briefly curtailed and then enlarged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a mood, picking up SAD. Shortened, SAD gives SA; expand those initials into the country they abbreviate.
explanation.definitionFit: This nation at the tip of Africa uses the initials SA.

clue.text: Put in a building for storage, by the way

indicators.note: by means beside, so the abbreviation for the way stands next to the rest

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a shed is a small building used for storing things

explanation.surface: Someone stored goods in an outbuilding, mentioning it in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' reads as a conversational aside, but 'the way' gives ST and 'by' places it beside A SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash something is to put it away out of sight, hidden for later.

clue.text: Low origins of Samson and Delilah

indicators.note: origins of asks for the opening letter of each of the three named words

explanation.surface: The humble beginnings of the biblical strongman and his betrayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Low in spirits means unhappy and downcast.

clue.text: Disconcert by positioning wood just below jack

indicators.note: in a down answer, just below puts the wood directly after the sailor

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is AB, able seaman
ash is a wood

explanation.surface: Unsettle someone by placing timber right underneath a lifting jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jack' looks like a lifting tool, but a jack tar is a sailor, AB.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to embarrass or make someone ill at ease.

clue.text: Ruth's all-round success

parts.note: Babe Ruth, the baseball great, had his triumphs when a hit let him run round every base

explanation.surface: Praise for a woman named Ruth who succeeds at everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth looks like a woman's name, but Babe Ruth was a legendary American baseball hitter.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball, a hit that lets the batter circle all the bases and score is the sport's big success.

clue.text: Girl's turning up in Hamlet, say, as female performer

indicators.note: in places the turned possessive inside the word for Hamlet's nationality

parts.note: Hamlet, Prince of Denmark, is an example of a Dane

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up reads the girl's name upward, so backwards

parts.note: Sue's, from the girl's name Sue

explanation.surface: A girl appears in a production of Hamlet as an actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' suggests a play or a village; he is a Dane. SUES turned up gives SEUS, set inside DANE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the French word for a female ballet dancer.

clue.text: Organize deliveries given one by Artful Dodger

definitions.meaning: to ... is to manage a delivery route, like a milk or paper round
a crafty evader gives you evasive, misleading treatment

explanation.surface: A milkman's rounds and a Dickensian pickpocket, the Artful Dodger from Oliver Twist.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as three words, it is to manage a delivery route; as one hyphenated noun, it is the evasion a dodger gives you. The Artful Dodger is the young thief in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a round means operating a regular delivery route; getting the runaround means being fobbed off with evasions.

clue.text: Capital man replaces woman in America

indicators.note: replaces says one stretch of the country's name is swapped out for the male word

parts.note: taken as the full country name
Erica is a woman's name, found at the end of the country's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A capital-letter Man takes the place of a woman somewhere in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: AMERICA ends in the woman's name ERICA; swap it for MAN and AM + MAN remains.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Jordan.

clue.text: Meeting-place for leaders of union militants

indicators.note: leaders of asks for the opening letter of each of the two following words

explanation.surface: Somewhere for trade union militant leaders to gather.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome the public square where citizens gathered was this, and it now means any place for discussion.

clue.text: Writer who ran the organization

indicators.note: organization signals that the letters of the preceding words are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An author who once headed the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organization' looks like a company but works as the anagram signal on WHO RAN THE. Nathaniel Hawthorne wrote The Scarlet Letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Hawthorne was a nineteenth-century American novelist, author of The Scarlet Letter.

clue.text: Fighting and training expert's book

parts.note: war is fighting
PE is physical education, training
an ace is an expert; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A combat-and-drill specialist has written a manual.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolstoy's epic novel of the Napoleonic wars has this title.

clue.text: Girl objects about long-distance vehicles

indicators.note: about means going around, so the girl and the objects together wrap the distance word

parts.note: Penny is a girl's name
things are objects
far means a long way off

explanation.surface: A girl raises objections to lorries that travel long distances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'objects' reads as a verb of protest but is the noun THINGS. PENNY + THINGS go around FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: These were early bicycles with one huge front wheel and a tiny rear one, named after two old British coins of different sizes.

clue.text: Sort of proposal not ready to be tabled?

definitions.meaning: not cooked enough to serve at the table

explanation.surface: A motion not yet prepared for formal discussion at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tabled' suggests putting a motion up for debate, but here it means served at the table, hence undercooked.
explanation.definitionFit: An ill-conceived plan is called undercooked, like food taken out of the oven too soon.

clue.text: Sounds like German port's catch is put under ship

indicators.note: Sounds like says the port's name is to be heard, then spelt another way

parts.note: Kiel is a port in northern Germany
a haul is a catch of fish

explanation.surface: A Baltic port's fishing catch is stowed below decks.
explanation.walkthrough: KIEL said aloud gives KEEL. The old naval punishment dragged a sailor under the hull.
explanation.definitionFit: Keelhauling was a brutal naval punishment of dragging a sailor beneath the hull from one side to the other.

clue.text: Teaching expert to take Eastern coin one catalogued

parts.note: a ducat is an old gold coin
I is the Roman numeral for one
something catalogued is entered on a list

explanation.surface: A teaching specialist is asked to take an oriental coin that has been itemised.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who specialises in the theory and methods of teaching is an expert in that field.

clue.text: Fool guy involved in study of flying saucers

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A foolish fellow gets drawn into researching alien spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: This field looks into reported sightings of alien spacecraft.

clue.text: Philosopher, in spring coming round in place of wizard

indicators.note: coming round means the spring word wraps around what follows

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
Oz is the land of the Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: A thinker strolling in springtime, coming round to the wizard's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a seventeenth-century Dutch rationalist philosopher.

clue.text: Plan to achieve aspiration with difficulty

definitions.meaning: a clever scheme or trick, in British slang
to breathe noisily and laboriously, aspiration being breathing

explanation.surface: A scheme for reaching one's ambitions despite obstacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition but means breathing. A 'wheeze' is also British slang for a crafty scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeze is British slang for a crafty scheme, and it also means breathing with a whistling rasp.

clue.text: Hurry to make appearance with instrument

indicators.note: with simply joins the two pieces side by side

parts.note: a person's looks are their appearance
the harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Rushing to turn up somewhere with a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make appearance' suggests arriving, but appearance just gives LOOKS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an imperative telling someone to be quick and alert.

clue.text: Authority to judge thus

parts.note: to say is to estimate or judge, as in I'd say it's ten miles
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: Power to pass judgment in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their permission or authoritative word.

clue.text: Ruthless captain appears as destroyer docked

indicators.note: docked means cut short, so the last letter of the word for destroyer is removed

parts.note: a blight is something that ruins or destroys

explanation.surface: A harsh naval commander shows up as a warship that has come into port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyer' and 'docked' suggest a warship in harbour; really BLIGHT loses its tail. Captain Bligh commanded HMS Bounty, whose crew mutinied.
explanation.definitionFit: William Bligh was the notoriously harsh commander of the Bounty, against whom the crew mutinied.

clue.text: Turn in unspecified sort of column

indicators.note: in places the word for a turn inside the word for unspecified

parts.note: any means no particular one, unspecified
a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: A rotation within some unnamed type of pillar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' suggests a pillar, but it is a newspaper column: the agony column carries readers' problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's agony column prints advice in reply to readers' personal problems.

clue.text: Author to extend industrial action

parts.note: to black goods is for a union to boycott them, a form of industrial action
to extend is to add more

explanation.surface: A writer is urged to prolong a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'black' is British trade-union slang for boycotting goods or work. R. D. Blackmore wrote Lorna Doone.
explanation.definitionFit: R. D. Blackmore was a Victorian novelist, best known for Lorna Doone.

clue.text: Don't allow to catch up

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word for catch reads upward, so backwards

parts.note: to nab is to catch

explanation.surface: An instruction forbidding someone to draw level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch up' looks like a phrasal verb but splits into NAB and the reversal signal 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ban something is to forbid or prohibit it.

clue.text: Record store in cellar

definitions.meaning: to put a track or performance on tape
to put wine away to mature

explanation.surface: A music shop in a basement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record store' looks like a music shop, but it splits into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians put tracks on tape this way, and wine buyers keep bottles to age with the same phrase.

clue.text: Last part of board meeting — endless agenda upset me

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order
endless means the final letter of the agenda word is cut off

explanation.surface: Wrapping up a directors' meeting, someone complains the agenda has annoyed them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts AGENDA to AGEND, and 'upset' shuffles AGEND + ME. 'board meeting' sounds corporate but means a chess game's board.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the final phase of a game, when few pieces remain, has this name.
